outline_method: Union of member StatCan 2025 CSD boundaries; full source precision retained, with unapproved member repairs propagated as unapproved regional candidates.

quebec_source.authority: Ministère des Ressources naturelles et des Forêts, Gouvernement du Québec
quebec_source.reference_date_note: Per-feature version V2026-08; exact boundary reference day is not supplied by this service.
quebec_source.exclusion_note: Separate additional source feature with code 09, retained in the source archive but not treated as an eighteenth region or added to the national outlines.

quebec_crosswalk_status: Geometric cross-check, not an independently approved official crosswalk. Review before production.

jurisdictions.reason: Numbered census divisions are a poor browsing choice. Tourism regions are promising, but a current reproducible boundary set and membership mapping still need qualification.
Three geographic counties; these browsing areas do not imply county governments.
Eighteen geographic counties. Halifax, Queens and Cape Breton county geography remains distinct from the similarly named regional municipalities.
Twelve regional service commission geographies from the post-reform 2025 source.
Seventeen régions administratives; a draft crosswalk groups the existing municipal outlines. MRCs are retained as source divisions, not substituted for administrative regions.

Forty named county, regional municipality and territorial district geographies. Nine generic census divisions are left without a region, including single-tier city equivalents. Separated cities and reserves in geographic counties do not become county-government members.
Economic, tourism and other regional schemes differ. Familiar areas such as Interlake and Parkland are candidates; a preferred complete boundary set needs qualification before importing.
Tourism travel zones and statistical divisions serve different purposes. A preferred complete geographic partition and reusable source need qualification.

Seven land-use regions are watershed-based planning units; numbered census divisions are another system. Defer choosing these as consumer regions until their usefulness for city/event browsing is reviewed.

Twenty-seven regional district geographies plus Stikine, explicitly typed as an unincorporated region. Northern Rockies remains at municipal level; its census division is not added as a duplicate regional district. These are geographic groupings, including separately governed Indigenous areas.
The census division duplicates the whole territory. Tourism regions exist, but their boundary source and grouping need qualification.
Named departmental regions differ from the six numbered census divisions. Defer until a specific current regional scheme and matching polygons are established.
Qikiqtaaluk, Kivalliq and Kitikmeot geographic regions. This does not model Inuit land ownership or governance.
